title: Bill Gates warns AI needs regulation like cars and medicine, says it can help prevent misuse
key_facts: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates wrote on X that AI needs safeguards like those that cover planes, cars and medicines.
He said such rules will not eliminate every harm but can help prevent misuse by bad actors.
In a CNN interview he said talk that all of humanity is at risk can get overblown, yet called AI more dangerous than cars, planes or drugs.
Last month he said AI could drive events that cause a billion deaths (India Today, no exact date).
Microsoft president Brad Smith told the BBC that a washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI.
Anthropic and OpenAI have argued for regulation; Meta and Nvidia are on the opposing side; President Trump has warned that regulating AI may let China win the race.
US tech leaders have signed Trump's AI accords, a voluntary, non-binding agreement on safe AI development.
India Today gives no dates for the X post or the CNN interview.
quote_evidence: "Just as we regulate planes, cars, and medicines, we need safeguards that help us realize AI's incredible potential while reducing the risks,”
“They won’t eliminate every harm, but they can help prevent misuse by bad actors,” he added.
“When people act like all of humanity is at risk in some intimate way, that is going too far."
why_it_matters_hint: Another prominent call for binding AI safety rules, with the industry split over regulation.
event_date: Dates of the X post and CNN interview are not stated; article published 12 Oct 2026.
notes: Remarks relayed from Gates's X post and a CNN interview. Gates made a similar call on NBC (27 Sep 2026) and in a New York Times interview (29 Sep 2026), both already in our 28 and 30 Sep editions.
